description:
DIAGNOSED (2026-07-02, at 0cb890e95); fix ready but BLOCKED BY fz-go4.18.29. This description is the authoritative state.

ROOT CAUSE (one mechanism family — arrival order becoming identity — two manifestations, only one semantic):
(b) SEMANTIC: same_call_target keys by CALLEE ONLY at two coalesce sites — semantic.rs:142 (summary store) and jobs/semantic.rs:1732 (emission merge; merge_target_activation resolves collisions first-arrival-wins). Two capture-variant activations of the same callee (repr_seam: the shared reduce-step wrapper fn160 demanded with the user-reducer arrow #65 AND Enum.count's predicate-wrapper arrow #162 from the same callsite) coalesce into one edge; arrival order tracks schedule; the callsite devirtualizes to the per-run winner; both dbg results route through one body -> output flips 10,10 <-> 2,2.
(a) BENIGN: Ty-id renaming across runs is presentation only (3-run structural-multiset comparison byte-identical; ids are within-run-consistent arrival names).
RESOLVED EN ROUTE: the orphaned provisional-arrow demand (append at a retracted arrow, 00001) NO LONGER OCCURS post-fz-go4.18.22 — that arc was demand-side and is fixed.

THE FIX (proven, preserved, withheld): call-target identity = callee + ACTIVATION at both sites. Measured: repr_seam deterministic in all modes; JIT/AOT go from 'no settled callable boundary' compile-error to RUNNING (deterministically wrong 10,10 — that residual is the f98.14 boundary bug, now with a clean signal). WITHHELD because it regresses opaque_fn_value_join::interp: a legitimately polymorphic joined callable (add_a/add_b) keeps two brand-only-distinct activations, and interp runtime dispatch (ir_interp/backend.rs:2600-2740) resolves by activation-input type overlap, which is BRAND-BLIND at runtime by design (fz-bsx) -> 'callable 163 ambiguous across entries'. PREREQUISITE: fz-go4.18.29 (value-identity dispatch at the boxed-callable boundary). Fix diff preserved in the session scratchpad (delta.diff).

DONE = after .18.29 lands: apply the two-site fix, red/green on repr_seam determinism (10-run distribution collapses to one answer), opaque_fn_value_join stays green, suite green 3x, clippy 0.

comments.text: Re-scoped context: schedule-dependent arrow keys are plausibly keys minted from MID-ASCENT demand values (the .18.22 founding defect). Post-.18.22 demand is deterministic (unique least fixpoint) — re-run the 2-run histogram diff on 00001 first; the orphaned provisional-arrow demand should also vanish. Diagnose only what survives.

Corroborating evidence from the fz-go4.18.22 rework (F2 root-cause): on fixtures2/behavior/repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2, the BackendProgram differs on every run of the same build — generated FunctionIds (161/162) swap between the two lambda executables and transport position orderings churn — and the interp answer flips {'10,10'|'2,2'} accordingly (both wrong; expected '10,2'; the two dbg callsites print one conflated closure result). Present identically on f92375bc6, 0810fcb89, and the F1-fixed rework; demand productions are 3/0-identical on all, so the non-determinism is in arrow/executable keying + backend assembly, not in RuntimeDemand.

RE-PRIORITIZED: after .18.22 (demand now byte-clean and schedule-stable), this is the DOMINANT open non-determinism. Fresh evidence from the .18.22 audits: repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2 flips its (wrong) answer 10,10 <-> 2,2 run-to-run on ALL commits (10-run distributions; two lambdas' generated FunctionIds 161/162 swap per run; BackendProgram dumps differ on every run of the same build); fz_f98 materialization wobbles at arrow Ty(319)/Ty(320) for FunctionId(174). Demand productions are 3/0-identical in every run while the OUTPUT varies — the non-determinism is squarely in activation-arrow/generated-id keying, not demand. The original 00001 histogram-diff evidence stands. Diagnose on the post-.18.22 trace (clean now).

PARTIAL (diagnosis agent stopped by owner mid-run, 2026-07-02): Q3 ANSWERED — the orphaned provisional-arrow demand (append demanded at a retracted arrow on 00001) NO LONGER OCCURS post-.18.22; the widen-then-retract arc was demand-side and is fixed. Remaining scope narrows to: (a) Ty-id renaming across runs (same structural arrow interned at different ids) and (b) the answer-changing seam (repr_seam lambda-id swap conflating reducer/predicate at a callable boundary). The agent's candidate fix direction at stop time (UNVERIFIED — treat as a lead, not a finding): 'make call-target identity variant-distinct (callee + activation) in the two coalesce sites.' Worktree preserved at agent-afe4ed67b73426813 (may contain instrumentation).

DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE (2026-07-02; full narrative in the agent report + prior comment). ROOT: arrival-order-becomes-identity at the two callee-only coalesce sites (semantic.rs:142, jobs/semantic.rs:1732 — merge_target_activation first-arrival-wins). Ty-id renaming confirmed BENIGN (structural multiset identical). FIX (callee+activation identity) proven correct but WITHHELD: regresses legitimately-polymorphic joined callables because interp runtime dispatch is brand-blind (fz-bsx) — now BLOCKED BY fz-go4.18.29 (value-identity dispatch at the boxed-callable boundary). Fix diff preserved in session scratchpad. Timing findings routed to .18.28: repr_seam interp 2.1-2.4s per run on a 6-line fixture (monolith family); full matrix exceeds 120s (384/386 at cap, stragglers enum_take_drop_split/enum_predicate_search build).
